about.title: About Me
about.bio_p1: I am an undergraduate at South China University of Technology (SCUT), majoring in Big Data Management and Application. My current research focuses on trustworthy medical AI, especially how ECG models use clinical evidence, how their behavior changes across datasets, and how physiological signals can be aligned with language.
about.bio_p2: Since January 2026, I have led a line of ECG research spanning matched-control evidence-use auditing, dataset-label evidence fingerprints, and knowledge-aware ECG–text representation learning. Two first-author manuscripts are currently under review at IEEE JBHI and BIBM 2026.
about.bio_p3: I also work at the AI Research Institute of Guangdong No. 2 Provincial People's Hospital, where I have contributed to medical LLMs, cardiovascular knowledge representation, clinical question answering, and deployable health-AI prototypes. Earlier projects include a standardized-patient system built from about 8,000 clinical cases and a myocardial-ischemia knowledge graph with interpretable machine-learning components.

projects.title: Projects
projects.subtitle: Research and systems at the intersection of AI, healthcare, and knowledge.

ecg_audit.title: Evidence-Use Auditing for Deep ECG Models
ecg_audit.desc_1: Developed a matched-control perturbation framework to audit whether deep ECG classifiers rely on clinically relevant evidence rather than task-correlated shortcuts.
ecg_audit.desc_2: Evaluated evidence use across PTB-XL and CODE-15%, multiple architectures, perturbation doses, and clinically defined evidence windows; manuscript under review at IEEE JBHI.

dlef.title: DLEF: Dataset-Label Evidence Fingerprints
dlef.desc_1: Proposed dataset-label evidence fingerprints to characterize how ECG evidence structure differs across datasets and diagnostic labels.
dlef.desc_2: Studied whether directional, boundary-aware fingerprints explain cross-dataset AUROC degradation across CODE-15%, PTB-XL, and Chapman-Shaoxing; manuscript under review at BIBM 2026.

pathclip.title: PathCLIP: Knowledge-Aware ECG–Text Representation Learning
pathclip.desc_1: Investigating whether diagnostic hierarchies and ECG findings improve ECG–text alignment, zero-shot recognition, and physiologically grounded representations.
pathclip.desc_2: Designed matched-count, permuted-hierarchy, residual-only, and held-out-label controls; current work shifts from ontology-only supervision toward finding grounding and evidence-aligned learning.
